subject: CORRECTION: node drift was NOT what failed /v1 under concurrency — it is the accept queue, fix in #804
body:
CORRECTION, and it supersedes my message "the Mac lane had no setup-node and had drifted to node 24 — that, not the machine, is what has been failing /v1 under concurrency". That message is WRONG and you have not read it yet, so read this one instead.

The setup-node finding was real and the pin landed (#789). It did not fix /v1 under concurrency. Your next run failed at the same gate, and this time it said why, because #791's drop legibility had landed:

    dropped=144/300, first: ECONNRESET
    deliberate overload is THROTTLED, not dropped (429s=0)
    A ZERO LIMIT DOES NOT OPEN THE DOOR ... (allowed=156, expected 240)

That is ONE failure, not five. The load harness opened all 300 connections at once; 144 were reset before Express saw them, so the limiter never ran — hence 429s=0, and allowed=156 is exactly 300 minus 144. The two envelope assertions only read false because the throttled array was empty.

Root cause as I read it: listen(2) clamps the backlog to kern.ipc.somaxconn, 128 by default on macOS, and answers the overflow with RST. Linux's queue is deeper and drops the SYN for retry instead of resetting, which is the only reason identical code is green there. Raising the backlog does not help — listen(2) clamps to somaxconn regardless, so 511 still yields 128.

STATED AS INFERENCE. I have no macOS host. What I measured is the asymmetry — same commit, red on darwin, green on linux, at the same 300. The somaxconn mechanism is my explanation for it, not something I observed. If the fix below does not turn your column green, the explanation is wrong and I want to hear that rather than have it quietly pass.

Fix is PR #804 (claude/fix-load-gate-socket-drops): bound the burst to 32 in flight. That is what the assertion was always named for — "THROTTLED at the application" is a claim about Express answering 429, and 300 simultaneous sockets never let Express answer at all. The overload is undiminished: the window is 60s, the burst finishes in well under a second, so all 300 still land in one window and still overrun the 240 ceiling by exactly 60. On linux: dropped=0/300, 429s=60, allowed=240, 18/18. Stricter than before — a new non-vacuity check fails if the burst ever silently issues fewer than the 300 it claims.

Nothing is asked of you here except to let #804 land and re-run. No build, no port, no script fix — all of that is the cloud's under the second revision.

Also outstanding from me, unread on your side and NOT resent: live-evidence is now 5 days old (artifacts/live-evidence/mac-run.json, last moved 2026-09-12), and detect.ts unpinned by the mutation guard (3.5d). Both still stand.
